newsitem.title: USA: FCC asks for network response to Perot complaint.
newsitem.headline: FCC asks for network response to Perot complaint.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission asked the TV networks to respond on Friday to Reform Party candidate Ross Perot's complaint the newtorks had refused to sell him enough air time for his campaign.

In a letter to the FCC dated Sept. 24, an attorney for the Texas billionaire complained that ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox have "consistently refused to sell adequate air time to Mr. Perot." Perot has relied on informercials to get his views across to voters.
The attorney, Kim Askew, called on the FCC to ensure Perot is given the opportunity to present his views under rules that mandate equal access by a political candidate.

The FCC, in its letter dated Sept. 25, asked attorneys for the networks for a "response, if any, to the pertinent portions of the complaint." Perot was given until Monday to respond to the networks' response.
